# TreeStore.splice drops grandchildren when adding an expanded subtree

## Context

Surfaced via standalone falsifier probe (`node --input-type=module` on `dev`) during review of `#21239` (`Resolves #21238`). While `#21238` fixes the crash when adding an expanded parent while `TreeStore` processes reactive configs (`_items === null`), this is an independent post-construction batch-ingestion defect in `TreeStore#splice`.

## The Problem

When a `TreeStore` already holds a projected expanded node (`unit-1`) and a caller appends a multi-level expanded subtree in a single `add()` batch (`[dept-1, person-1]`), `person-1` is recorded in `#allRecordsMap` and `#childrenMap` (`store.getCount() === 3`), but **dropped from the flat `_items` projection (`store.count === 2`)**:

```javascript
import Neo       from './src/Neo.mjs';
import * as core from './src/core/_export.mjs';
import TreeStore from './src/data/TreeStore.mjs';
import TreeModel from './src/data/TreeModel.mjs';

Neo.config.unitTestMode = true;

class M extends TreeModel {
    static config = {
        className: 'Probe.Model',
        fields   : [{name: 'id', type: 'String'}, {name: 'name', type: 'String'}]
    }
}
const Model = Neo.setupClass(M);

const store = Neo.create(TreeStore, {
    model: Model,
    data : [{id: 'unit-1', name: 'Unit', isLeaf: false, collapsed: false}]
});

store.add([
    {id: 'dept-1',   name: 'Dept',   parentId: 'unit-1', isLeaf: false, collapsed: false},
    {id: 'person-1', name: 'Person', parentId: 'dept-1', isLeaf: true}
]);

// Observed: ['unit-1', 'dept-1'] (allRecordsMap size: 3, projected count: 2)
// Expected: ['unit-1', 'dept-1', 'person-1']
```

Observed on `dev` (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs`, same behavior before and after `#21239`).

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1152-1258` splits `splice()` additions into step `2a` (ingesting each item into `#allRecordsMap` and `#childrenMap`) and step `2b` (projecting `newRoots` via `collectVisibleDescendants` at lines `1248-1257` *after* `#childrenMap` is complete).
- For any item whose parent already exists in `#allRecordsMap` (`else` branch at lines `1232-1244`), step `2a` calls `me.collectVisibleDescendants(data, visibleToAdd)` **mid-loop** during `i = 0` (`dept-1`):
  1. At `i = 0`, `'person-1'` has not yet entered `#childrenMap.get('dept-1')`, so `collectVisibleDescendants(dept-1, visibleToAdd)` pushes only `'dept-1'`.
  2. At `i = 1`, `'person-1'` joins `#childrenMap.get('dept-1')`, and its `else` branch checks `me.map?.has('dept-1')` (or `me.indexOf(parentNode) > -1` before `#21239`). Because `'dept-1'` sits in `visibleToAdd` waiting for `super.splice()` at line `1318`, both checks return `false`, so `'person-1'` is skipped completely.
- Conversely, if `'person-1'` appeared before `'dept-1'` in the input array, `'person-1'` would see no `#allRecordsMap.get('dept-1')` at `i = 0` and be wrongly auto-healed to `'root'` (`lines 1209-1231`). `#21238`'s construction case only masked the bug because initial construction starts with an empty `#allRecordsMap`, routing `unit-1` through `newRoots` into step `2b`.

Design authority: n/a — concrete projection data-loss defect reproduced on `dev` via standalone `TreeStore` probe above.

## The Fix

Decouple structural ingestion from visible projection inside `TreeStore#splice` (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1152-1258`):

1. **Complete step `2a` across all `items` before calling `collectVisibleDescendants` on any item**, recording candidate subtrees whose pre-existing projected ancestor (`me.map?.has(parentId)`) was already visible before the batch (excluding descendants whose ancestor was also ingested in the same batch, since collecting the top added node in step `2b` traverses the full `#childrenMap` subtree once).
2. **In step `2b`, project all top-level visible additions (`newRoots` and newly visible subtrees under existing projected parents)** after `#childrenMap` holds every node in the batch, preserving tree order and target `insertIndex`. (Respect `#21239`'s `me.map?.has(...)` check when `_items` is `null` during reactive construction.)

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Adding a multi-level expanded subtree (`[dept, person]` as well as 3+ levels `[dept, team, person]`) via `store.add([...])` under an already-projected expanded parent (`unit-1`) projects every visible descendant (`['unit-1', 'dept-1', 'person-1']`), matching initial `data` load and sequential `add()` calls.
- [ ] A collapsed intermediate parent (`dept.collapsed: true`) added in the same batch still projects only `'dept-1'` (`['unit-1', 'dept-1']`) until explicitly expanded.
- [ ] No node is duplicated in `_items` / `visibleToAdd` when multiple expanded levels arrive together.
- [ ] Added unit cases under `test/playwright/unit/data/` fail on `dev` and pass at head, and `test/playwright/unit/data/TreeStore*.spec.mjs` stays green.

## Out of Scope

- Out-of-order parent-after-child disconnected root reparenting (`lines 1209-1231`), unless clean two-pass ingestion handles it without breaking existing disconnected-node tests.
- Turbo Mode raw re-add + `updateRows` reprojection (`#21008`) and `'root'` ID key collision (`defect-note` `b0454c89`).

## Avoided Traps

- **Collecting on `i = 1` by checking `visibleToAdd.includes(parentNode)` without checking duplicate collection or `insertIndex`:** If a grandchild (`dept -> team -> person`) or sorted/filtered projection is involved, ad-hoc array scans miss multi-level ordering and risk `O(N^2)` in bulk loads. Deferring `collectVisibleDescendants` until step `2b` keeps traversal single-pass over `#childrenMap`.

- 2026-11-17T14:10:35Z @tobiu referenced in commit `fd71bfd` - "fix(data): a subtree added in one batch projects all its levels (#21252) (#21255)

TreeStore#splice collected an attached node's visible descendants while
it was still ingesting the batch. Children that followed the node in the
same add() were not in #childrenMap yet, and the projected-parent check
skipped them later because their parent was only queued, not projected.
Adding [dept (expanded), person] under an expanded unit showed dept
without person.

Step 2a now records those nodes and computes the insert index where it
did; step 2b collects their subtrees once the whole batch is ingested.
Insert positions are unchanged. The new spec fails two of four arms on
dev, and 1194 data, collection and grid unit specs pass."
